{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABXaDRbA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhA-JZ0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 9, "title": "Consolidate emulated devices to Meta Quest 3 and generic Android phone", "body": "## Problem

The emulator currently exposes many legacy headset profiles (Cardboard, Vive, Oculus Go/Rift/Quest/Quest 2, Gear VR), a legacy Samsung Galaxy S8+ AR profile, and a "None" profile. This expands the UI, test matrix, and maintenance burden before work on modern WebXR API conformance. The old profile names and device-specific assumptions do not reflect the intended modern development targets.

## Expected outcome

Expose **exactly two selectable device profiles** in the DevTools device picker:

1. **Meta Quest 3** — representative standalone 6DoF headset with two tracked controllers, supporting the existing immersive VR behavior and a usable immersive AR/MR mode switch within the *same profile*.
2. **Generic Android Phone (ARCore)** — generic 6DoF handheld Android AR emulator with touch/transient input and the existing virtual-room/hit-test behavior; do not bind the profile to an obsolete Samsung model.

Default to Meta Quest 3. The user must be able to choose VR or MR when the Quest profile is selected, without introducing a third device profile. Keep the existing inline mode where applicable. This Issue reorganizes profiles and preserves currently supported functionality; it **does not** claim to implement physical-device-specific fidelity or new WebXR features (e.g. hand tracking, anchors, depth sensing), which belong to future API-conformance issues.

## Context

- Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), and the repository PR template. Write Issue/PR/commit text in English, base work on `dev`, and target `dev`.
- `src/devices.json` currently contains the old profiles and defaults to `Oculus Quest`. `src/ConfigurationManager.ts` loads/saves the selected device, and `src/app/panel.ts` controls device selection, stereo, poses, controllers, and rendering. `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts` currently distinguishes AR from VR through device modes, and `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts` implements the existing handheld AR room/tablet.
- Quest VR and Quest MR must be selectable as **session/emulation modes of one device**, not two duplicate profiles. Inspect and adjust assumptions that infer the active emulation mode solely from whether a device supports `immersive-ar`; preserve correct view/pose/input behavior when both immersive modes are advertised. If a session-mode control is required, keep it separate from the device picker and clearly label it.
- The current Android AR representation uses virtual pointer/tablet internals for touch. Those implementation details may remain where necessary, but the public profile and UI should represent a phone rather than a headset with two physical controllers.
- Preserve the TypeScript, Three.js r186, Chrome Manifest V3, Firefox packaging, and current packaged local assets. Do not add unrelated new WebXR API implementations or claim real-device fidelity.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Update `src/devices.json` to contain **only** `Meta Quest 3` and `Generic Android Phone (ARCore)` as selectable device profiles; remove legacy profile entries, including `None`, and set the default to Quest 3. Keep valid `inline` session behavior where supported.
- [ ] Provide Quest 3 immersive VR and immersive AR/MR **within the single Quest profile**. If a mode selector is needed, make it explicit, usable, and persistent as appropriate. Correct mode-dependent logic, including stereo/monoscopic views, virtual-room presentation, input semantics, and session lifecycle, without assuming all Quest sessions are AR simply because AR is supported.
- [ ] Preserve Quest 3's two tracked controllers and their existing select/squeeze input, headset/controller 6DoF pose manipulation, and VR stereo rendering. Use accurate naming without claiming emulated features that are not implemented.
- [ ] Provide the Android phone's existing handheld AR experience: 6DoF camera movement, screen/touch input, virtual-room rendering, and persistent/transient hit testing. Keep internal virtual controls as needed but avoid misleading physical-controller UI for the phone.
- [ ] Update `src/ConfigurationManager.ts`, relevant shared TypeScript types, DevTools panel UI, and event/message handling so selecting either profile and changing the Quest mode works across reloads, with sensible fallback/migration from previously saved removed profile IDs.
- [ ] Update existing browser regression fixtures/tests that reference `Oculus Quest`, `HTC Vive`, or `Samsung Galaxy S8+ (AR)`. Verify both new profiles, Quest VR/MR mode selection, persistence, pose/gizmo and select/squeeze, Android AR touch/hit tests, worker restart/frame routing, and first-script WebXR availability. Test mode switches and ending/restarting sessions.
- [ ] Run and document `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, and `npm run test:browser` on a current compatible desktop Chrome/Chromium build; report actual outcomes and any existing limitations. Visually inspect the updated DevTools panel and both immersive modes where practical.
- [ ] Update README device tables, usage guidance, and developer notes to reflect exactly two profiles, explain the Quest VR/MR switch and Android AR simulation, and distinguish emulated API behavior from real Quest 3/ARCore hardware capability.
- [ ] Submit a focused implementation PR against `dev` using the repository template and request review. No intentionally deferred portion of this profile-consolidation scope should be described as completed.

## Optional validation

- Run Firefox MV3 runtime regression checks if a supported Firefox installation is available.
- Test representative WebXR samples in Quest VR/MR and Android AR configurations.

## Required post-merge verification

None. The required functional, build, and browser checks are pre-merge validation; store publication is out of scope.
